clue.text: Right time, on reflection, to make choice

indicators.note: reflection reverses an image, so the word for time is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone waits for the right moment, after some thought, to make a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choice' reads like a decision, but here it is the adjective for something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of exceptionally fine quality, as in a choice or rare vintage.

clue.text: No choice?

definitions.meaning: saying no is turning something down
the option to take or decline something

explanation.definitionFit: A rejection is a plain no, and first refusal is the option or choice offered before anyone else.

clue.text: Bones set differently at last

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Bones set differently at last (5)', has no fodder that rearranges to give the letters of the answer; part of the clue appears lost in OCR and no source gives it.

clue.text: Crude painting without a name

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the naming word goes round the article

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name

explanation.surface: An amateur canvas is left unsigned, with no artist named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: DUB is placed around A. It looks like 'lacking', which would point at a deletion instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear of paint applied clumsily is the noun for an unskilled picture.

clue.text: Frank statement in a letter read out

indicators.note: reading something out means it is spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: A, E, I, O and U are each a vowel, a kind of letter

explanation.surface: An honest declaration is made in correspondence and then recited aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' says 'a vowel' is heard rather than spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: An open declaration or confession is a candid admission made publicly.

clue.text: Officer in parliament found in bar repeatedly

parts.note: bar is used twice: to blacklist is to bar someone
the second bar is a rod, a metal bar

explanation.surface: A parliamentary official keeps turning up in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' asks for two different synonyms of 'bar', one to ban and one a stick. Black Rod is the official who summons MPs to the House of Lords at the State Opening of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer of the House of Lords is a ceremonial official of the UK legislature.

clue.text: Cast out of never-ending paradise

indicators.note: never-ending tells us the word for paradise loses its final letter

parts.note: heaven is paradise

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of a paradise that turns out not to be eternal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' docks the last letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast something is to throw or hurl it, which is the verb meaning to lift and throw hard.

clue.text: Severely modified UK contract presented tricky problem

parts.note: to hit hard is to hit severely

indicators.note: something modified has been changed, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British agreement heavily revised turns out to be a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges UKCONTRACT into NUTTOCRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult puzzle or person that resists solution is described by this idiom about a tough shell.

clue.text: Fear capture

definitions.meaning: to dread or be anxious about something to come

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to anticipate with dread, as in apprehension, and to arrest a suspect.

clue.text: Old record on writer and sculptor

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is an old format of record
Gertrude Stein was an American writer

explanation.surface: A vintage disc sits on top of an author and an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts EP above STEIN. Jacob Epstein was a British sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein was a twentieth-century British artist who carved and modelled statues.

clue.text: Vainly try to sell commercials about English shire?

parts.note: to flog something is slang for selling it

indicators.note: about means around, so the pair of adverts surround the letter for English

parts.note: two adverts, each an AD
a shire is a breed of heavy horse

explanation.surface: A doomed sales pitch uses adverts for an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places E inside AD AD. 'shire' looks like a county but is the horse breed, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to waste effort on a cause that is already lost.

clue.text: WI leader, one with love for opera

parts.note: Fidel Castro led Cuba, in the West Indies
I is the Roman numeral one
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: The head of the Women's Institute is a single woman who loves opera.
explanation.walkthrough: WI suggests the Women's Institute, a British women's club; here it is the West Indies, whose leader is Fidel Castro.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's only stage work is a famous German opera.

clue.text: One of the pack's very big and fit

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the rugby scrum, or pack
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A rugby forward is huge and in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the forwards are called the pack, and a prop is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apposite or appropriate is suitable, which is what fit means as an adjective.

clue.text: Advice to angler catching tiddler or woman's shoe?

definitions.meaning: an angler with a tiny fish is told to throw it back
a shoe with a strap round the back of the heel

explanation.definitionFit: A strappy shoe with an open back is held by a band round the heel.

clue.text: Sweetheart welcomed by kind relation

indicators.note: being welcomed means being taken in, so the heart letter goes inside the word for kind

parts.note: kind means nice
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A lover is warmly received by a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a lover but is the centre letter of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family relative.

clue.text: Greek character wanting, a sexy…, dance

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the dance is missing one A

parts.note: the lambada is a sensual Brazilian dance

explanation.surface: A Greek man wishes for a sexy dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like desire but means lacking: LAMBADA loses an A.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet is a character in that script.

clue.text: Fellow works to get into an advantageous position

parts.note: a fellow is a man
oeuvre is an artist's body of works

explanation.surface: A man labours to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To manoeuvre is to move skilfully so as to gain a tactical edge.

clue.text: He runs to get free in this direction

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An escapee flees to gain freedom this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges HERUNSTO, with 'get' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying toward or coming from the south describes a compass bearing.

clue.text: Sounded like ref in the game was in …charge

parts.note: whist is a card game
led means was in charge

explanation.surface: The referee blew his instrument during a match he controlled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the game' is the card game, not the match the referee is running.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee blows a whistle, so making that sound is what one does.

clue.text: Ban Shute novel? One who likes Browning might

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made new in another order

explanation.surface: Banning a Nevil Shute book? A fan of the poet Browning might.
explanation.walkthrough: Nevil Shute was a novelist and Robert Browning a poet, but 'Browning' here means getting a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanning in the sun is what someone keen on a brown skin would do.

clue.text: Search around London area for Liverpudlian

indicators.note: around means the search word wraps round the London area

parts.note: to scour is to search thoroughly
SE is the south-east London postal district

explanation.surface: A hunt across London for someone from Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scouser is a native of Liverpool, a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Liverpool is called by this nickname, from the local stew lobscouse.

clue.text: Arrange for bishop to lead march

indicators.note: to lead means to go in front, so the bishop's letter comes first

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
to order is to arrange

explanation.surface: A bishop is lined up to head a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'march' looks like a parade but is the noun for frontier land, as in the Welsh Marches.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is a frontier region between two territories.

clue.text: Especially good and varied collection of hymns

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Especially good and varied collection of hymns (7)': the only parse is G plus the letters of 'varied' rearranged, with 'varied' as both fodder and anagram indicator; 'Especially' has no job.
annotationWithheld.clue: Especially good and varied collection of hymns

clue.text: Announced measures needed to find mineral

indicators.note: something announced is spoken, so the word for measures is heard rather than seen

parts.note: quarts are measures of liquid

explanation.surface: Measurements are declared necessary to locate a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announced' says QUARTS is heard, giving the mineral spelt with a Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystalline silica is a common rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Honour a husband? It works like a charm

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Decorating a husband turns out to be magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a Caribbean folk sorcery practised through spells and fetishes, magic working as charms do.

clue.text: One in position to catch out Conservative and Labour leader, say

definitions.text: One in position to catch out

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for for example, which say means

explanation.surface: Someone poised to trap a Tory and the head of the Labour party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' and 'Labour' suggest British politics; here they are a stuffy person and a first letter. Square leg is a fielding position in cricket, beside the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: This fielder in cricket stands where a batsman may be caught.

clue.text: Scream coming from Slaughterhouse 5 characters

indicators.note: coming from says the letters are drawn out of the word that follows, five of them

explanation.surface: A shriek emerges from five characters in Vonnegut's novel Slaughterhouse-Five.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 characters' plays on the novel title Slaughterhouse-Five and tells the length of the run taken from within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is informal for something hilarious, a real hoot.

clue.text: Different girl always being embraced

indicators.note: being embraced means held inside, so the word for always goes within the girl's name

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name
ever means always

explanation.surface: A distinctive girl is forever being hugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' is the old sense of the answer, meaning separate, not the modern 'a few'.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense the word means separate or distinct, as in going their several ways.

clue.text: Anchorite's corrupting 'influence recalled by half of sect

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ulcer is figuratively a corrupting influence

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A hermit is a corrupting influence remembered by a split religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns ULCER into RECLU; 'half of' gives SE from 'sect'. The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious hermit who lives shut away from the world.

clue.text: Still not finished going on about magistrate

indicators.note: going on means being placed after, so the shortened word follows

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: not finished says the word for still loses its final letter

parts.note: even means still, as in even more

explanation.surface: Someone continues to grumble about a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was a medieval English local official; 'Still' must be read as the adverb, as in 'even better'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or chief magistrate in medieval England.

clue.text: Shock announcement from the Times?

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word for times is heard

parts.note: days means times, as in the old days

explanation.surface: A startling statement issued by The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Times' looks like the newspaper that printed the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed state is stunned bewilderment, which shock produces.

clue.text: Bird's tail talked about

indicators.note: talked about means spoken, so the word for tail is heard

parts.note: the rear is the tail end

explanation.surface: A bird's tail is the subject of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent REAR and the bird's name sound alike. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird.
